**Finding: COMPLIANT (sits at the fallback) — no redline proposed.**

- **Nature of the document:** a securitization transfer and servicing agreement; there is no software, deliverable or licensed technology, so the software-conformance element has no subject matter. The "services" are Cellco's servicing of the Receivables.
- **Services warranty / duration:** Section 3.2(a) imposes an express industry-standard servicing standard (reasonable care, same degree of skill and attention as for comparable receivables it services for itself or others, per the Servicing Procedures), and Section 6.1(a) reps — including compliance with Law and material compliance with the Servicing Procedures — are given as of the Closing Date **and each Acquisition Date** and expressly survive transfer. That is continuous coverage, far exceeding the 30-day fallback floor.
- **Repair/replacement:** Section 3.3(b) notice-and-correct mechanic; Section 7.2(a)(ii) permits removal and replacement of the Servicer for uncured failures with material adverse effect.
- **Refund:** Sections 2.5 and 3.3(d) compel reacquisition/acquisition of affected Receivables at the Acquisition Amount — the economic refund analogue.
- **No walk-away risk:** there is no "AS IS" or warranty disclaimer; the only no-warranty language (Section 3.3(e)) runs in our favour, since it is the Issuer transferring without recourse.
- **Noted, not flagged:** no express professional/workmanlike or no-malicious-code warranty (preferred-only), and the reacquisition remedies are stated as sole remedies. The willful misconduct / bad faith / gross negligence liability floor in Section 6.2(a) is a limitation-of-liability issue and is left to that rule rather than double-flagged here.
